He briefly joined Hồ Chí Minh's Việt Minh in 1945 before becoming president of South Vietnam, a post he held until resigning days before the fall of Saigon — who was he?
Nguyễn Văn Thiệu: President of South Vietnam from 1967 to 1975.
A KGB colonel who secretly fed intelligence to MI6 for over a decade, this double agent was smuggled out of the Soviet Union in 1985 under the code name Operation Pimlico — who is he?
Oleg Gordievsky: KGB colonel and double agent (1938–2025)
Founded in 698 by Tae Choyŏng and originally called the Kingdom of Jin, which multiethnic realm once spanned Northeast China, the northern Korean Peninsula, and the Russian Far East?
Parhae: 7th-10th century kingdom in East Asia.
This Free-French general was made a Marshal of France posthumously in 1952 — yet his countrymen know him by a single name. Who was this World War II commander?
Philippe Leclerc de Hauteclocque: French general (1902–1947)
Published in 2023 by the Heritage Foundation, which initiative pairs a 'Mandate for Leadership' policy document with a loyalist-staffing database to consolidate executive power?
Project 2025: Conservative political initiative in the United States.
The oldest of 14 children born to Palestinian immigrants in Detroit, this congresswoman became the first Palestinian American woman elected to Congress in 2018 — who is she?
Rashida Tlaib: American politician and lawyer (born 1976)
Co-leading Germany's Greens alongside Annalena Baerbock, this politician served as Vice Chancellor and climate minister under Chancellor Olaf Scholz — who is he?

Over three days in September 1982, Lebanese Forces militiamen — backed by the IDF — killed thousands of mostly Palestinian and Shia civilians in a Beirut neighbourhood and adjacent refugee camp; what is this atrocity called?
Sabra and Shatila massacre: 1982 mass murder of civilians in Beirut, Lebanon.
This Finnish lawyer chaired the National Coalition Party from 1994 to 2001 and later served as president from 2012 to 2024, defeating Pekka Haavisto in a 2012 runoff — who is he?
Sauli Niinistö: President of Finland from 2012 to 2024. Sauli Väinämö Niinistö (born 24 August 1948) is a Finnish politician who served as the president of Finland from 2012 to 2024.
After serving as Islam Karimov's prime minister, this politician became president of Uzbekistan in 2016 and later chaired the Organization of Turkic States — who is he?
Shavkat Mirziyoyev: President of Uzbekistan since 2016. Shavkat Miromonovich Mirziyoyev (born 24 July 1957) is an Uzbek politician who has served as the second president of Uzbekistan since 2016.
Depicted in the Buddhist wheel of existence, these realms — from gods and humans to hungry ghosts and hell — are where beings are reborn according to their karma. What is it called?
Six Paths: Concept in Buddhist cosmology.
His was the longest reign of any Ottoman sultan, taking Belgrade in 1521 and Rhodes in 1522 and shattering Hungary's army at Mohács in 1526 — who was this sultan?
Suleiman the Magnificent: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (1520–1566)
Also called the Decalogue, these covenant directives were given to Moses atop Mount Sinai and later smashed after he found the Israelites worshipping a golden calf. What are they?
Ten Commandments: Biblical principles relating to ethics and worship.
Ten days before the 1968 Summer Olympics opened as scheduled, Mexican armed forces opened fire on unarmed student protesters in a Mexico City plaza — what is this event called?
Tlatelolco massacre: 1968 killing of anti-government protestors by the Mexican Armed Forces in Mexico City.

Centered on the Armenian highlands between three great lakes and locked in frequent wars with Assyria, this Iron Age kingdom left behind cuneiform inscriptions and massive fortresses before falling to the Medes or Cyrus the Great — what kingdom was it?
Urartu: Iron-Age kingdom of the ancient Near East.
Born in Leningrad and working 16 years as a KGB foreign intelligence officer, this politician has served as the de facto Russian leader since 1999 — who is he?
Vladimir Putin: President of Russia (2000–2008; since 2012)
Canada's first French-Canadian prime minister, he served 15 unbroken years from 1896 and built his legacy on compromise between English and French Canada — who is he?
Wilfrid Laurier: Prime Minister of Canada from 1896 to 1911. Sir Henri Charles Wilfrid Laurier (November 20, 1841 – February 17, 1919) was the seventh prime minister of Canada from 1896 to 1911.
A computer engineer by training, this Mexican senator and former Mexico City borough mayor ran as a coalition's nominee for the 2024 presidential election. Who is she?
An electrical engineer who was branded a "rightist" for criticizing Mao's economic policies during the Hundred Flowers Campaign, he went on to serve as China's premier from 1998 to 2003 — who is he?
Zhu Rongji: Premier of China from 1998 to 2003. Born in Changsha, Hunan, Zhu became a member of the CCP in 1949, the same year the People's Republic of China was established.
Who among these was born first?
Joseph Schumpeter (born 1883) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?

Ivan Pavlov (born 1849) is the earliest of the four. Pavlov also conducted significant research on the physiology of digestion, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1904.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Bruno Rossi is an astronomer. Bruno Benedetto Rossi ( ROSS-ee, Italian: [ˈbruːno beneˈdetto ˈrossi]; 13 April 1905 – 21 November 1993) was an Italian-American experimental physicist.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Hilary Putnam is a mathematician. Outside philosophy, Putnam contributed to mathematics and computer science.
What is the atomic number of Indium?
Indium: It is a silvery-white post-transition metal and one of the softest elements.
What is the atomic number of Scandium?
Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
In what year was Stephen Hawking born?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year was Richard Sackler born?
Richard Sackler: Sackler and Purdue's role in the epidemic led to many lawsuits and fines, with the company filing bankruptcy in 2019.
In what year was Aristotle born?
Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year did Abraham Maslow die?
Abraham Maslow: Maslow was a psychology professor at Cornell University, Brooklyn College, Brandeis University, The New School for Social Research, and Columbia University.
In what year did Kevin Mitnick die?
Kevin Mitnick: Kevin David Mitnick (August 6, 1963 – July 16, 2023) was an American computer security consultant, author, and convicted hacker.
In what year was Mass–energy equivalence discovered?
Mass–energy equivalence: In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Which company manufactures Harrier jump jet?
Harrier jump jet: Hawker Siddeley. The Harrier emerged as the only truly successful V/STOL design of the many attempted during that era.
NHIndustries NH90: Airbus Helicopters. The NHIndustries NH90 is a medium-sized European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter.
Which country is Hawker Hunter from?
Hawker Hunter: United Kingdom. The all-weather/night fighter role was filled by the Gloster Javelin.
Who is credited with discovering Bohrium?
Bohrium: Yuri Oganessian. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Who is credited with discovering 10 Hygiea?
10 Hygiea: Annibale de Gasparis. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Who is credited with discovering Nickel?
Nickel: Axel Fredrik Cronstedt. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Home to both edible and poisonous species, this fungal genus supplies the West's most popular cultivated mushrooms, including the everyday button mushroom — which genus is it?
Agaricus is a genus of mushroom-forming fungi containing both edible and poisonous species, with over 400 members worldwide and possibly again as many disputed or newly discovered species.

This central nervous system stimulant treats ADHD and narcolepsy today, but was once prescribed for nasal congestion and depression, and remains tightly controlled due to its abuse potential — name the drug?

Amphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy; it is also used to treat binge eating disorder in the form of lisdexamfetamine.
Marked by right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and fever, this common inflammatory condition is typically caused by a blockage from a small hard mass called a fecalith — name the condition?
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.
Present in every living cell and abundant in liver and meats, this B vitamin acts as an enzyme cofactor and takes its name from the Greek for 'life' — what is it?
Biotin (also known as vitamin B7 and vitamin H) is one of the B vitamins - a group of essential dietary micronutrients.

David Attenborough called this English particle physicist the natural successor for the BBC's scientific programming, thanks to shows like The Infinite Monkey Cage and his Wonders of... series — who is he?
Brian Cox (physicist) (born 3 March 1968) is an English physicist and musician.

Ranging from 9 to 20 centimeters long and known on the Italian mainland by a slightly different name, this Sicilian pastry features a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with a sweet ricotta cream — which pastry?
Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
First flown in 1998, this Chinese-built multirole combat aircraft features a delta wing and canard design and is nicknamed "Vigorous Dragon" — which fighter jet is it?

Chengdu J-10 (pinyin: Jian-Shi), also known as Menglong (pinyin: Menglong; lit. 'Vigorous Dragon'), is a Chinese medium-weight, single-engine, multirole combat aircraft with a delta wing and canard design.
Domed-backed little beetles that mostly hunt aphids, they wear aposematic spots to warn off predators and are named for 'lady' Mary — what's the scientific family?
Coccinellidae is a widespread family of small beetles.
This blood-feeding parasitic insect usually lives in human pubic hair and is thought to have diverged from a closely related gorilla parasite roughly 3.3 million years ago — what is it?
Crab louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
This Asian canid stands apart from true dogs: a convex rather than concave skull, no third lower molar, and single-cusped upper molars — once it roamed into Europe. What is it?
Dhole (dohl; Cuon alpinus) is a canid native to South, East and Southeast Asia.
Long used in traditional Indigenous medicine, this prairie-dwelling genus of purple daisy relatives gets its name from a Greek word meaning 'hedgehog' — what plant is it?
Echinacea is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the daisy family.
Comprising around 50 species mostly found in the tropics, this fungal genus infects rye, wheat, barley, and other grasses, producing toxic alkaloids — name the group of fungi?
Ergot is a group of fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).
Also badged as the Citroën Jumper and the Peugeot Boxer in Europe, this light commercial van entered North America in 2014 as the Ram ProMaster — which van?
Fiat Ducato is a light commercial vehicle jointly developed by FCA Italy and PSA Group (now Stellantis), and mainly manufactured by Sevel, a joint venture between the two companies since 1981.

A bulbous Allium native to Central Asia and northeastern Iran, this kitchen staple counts the chive, leek, and shallot among its cousins and was prized by ancient Babylonians and Egyptians — what is it?
Garlic (Allium sativum) is a species of bulbous flowering plants in the genus Allium.
This system of rules governs how a language is structured, covering everything from word order to the deeper study of sounds, meaning, and sentence formation — what is it called?
Grammar is the system of rules that governs how a natural language is structured and used, as evidenced by its speakers or writers.
Living to the age of 104, this French pioneer of algebraic topology was also the son-in-law of physicist Pierre Weiss and the eldest of a remarkable scientific brood — who was he?
Henri Cartan (8 July 1904 - 13 August 2008) was a French mathematician who made substantial contributions to algebraic topology.
Often caused by kidney failure or certain blood-pressure medications, this condition means too much potassium in the blood, with levels above 5.5 mmol/L — what's it called?
Hyperkalemia is an elevated level of potassium (K+) in the blood.
This mild oxidizing agent and Lewis acid, with the formula FeCl3, is commonly used to purify water and to etch metal surfaces — which compound is it?
Iron(III) chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula FeCl3. The anhydrous derivative is a Lewis acid, while all forms are mild oxidizing agents.

He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987 and ran twice for the Libertarian presidential nomination — yet later urged people to uninstall the very product that still bears his name. Who is he?
John McAfee (18 September 1945 - 23 June 2021) was a British and American computer programmer, businessman, and two-time U.S.
Built from four fused rings, compounds in this class include cholesterol, testosterone, and anti-inflammatory drugs like dexamethasone. What class of compound is it?
Kurt Gödel (April 28, 1906 - January 14, 1978) was a logician, mathematician, cosmologist, and philosopher.

First isolated from linseed oil and named from the Latin words for 'flax' and 'oil,' this omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid is one of the two essential fats humans must get from their diet — which acid?
Linoleic acid (LA) is an organic compound with the formula CH3(CH2)4CH=CHCH2CH=CH(CH2)7COOH.

A chemical element with symbol Mg and atomic number 12, it's a shiny gray metal with low density and high chemical reactivity that readily reacts with air to form a thin passivation oxide coating. What element is this?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12. The free metal burns with a brilliant-white light.
First synthesized in 1982 near Darmstadt, this fleeting synthetic element of the periodic table's seventh period was named in 1997 after a pioneering Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist. What is it?
Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
This New World songbird mimics the calls of other species, insects, and frogs, and serves as the state bird of five U.S. states — which bird?
Mockingbird are a group of New World passerine bird from the family Mimidae.

This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, attacking REM sleep with daytime drowsiness, sleep paralysis, and cataplexy — sudden episodes where muscle tone simply vanishes. What is it?
Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep-wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.

This biochemical process by which living things use food and water to sustain life can go wrong in either direction, causing malnutrition from either too much or too little of an essential compound — what process is it?
Nutrition is the biochemical and physiological process by which an organism uses food and water to support its life.

Covered in large protective keratin scales, these mammals — sometimes called scaly anteaters — range across Asia and sub-Saharan Africa and are the only mammal order known to have such scales — what are they?
Pangolin are mammals of the order Pholidota. The one extant family, the Manidae, has three genera: Manis, Phataginus, and Smutsia.
Which management theorist and educator's writings on organizing business, government, and nonprofit sectors made him one of the most influential thinkers on modern management?

Peter Drucker (November 19, 1909 - November 11, 2005) was an Austrian American management consultant, educator, and author, whose writings contributed to the philosophical and practical foundations of modern management theory.
Known as greater plantain, this Eurasian-native flowering plant is often confused by name with a banana relative, despite no real botanical connection between the two. Which species is it?
Plantago major is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae.
A byproduct of natural gas processing and petroleum refining, this three-carbon gas becomes liquid under pressure and is a key component of the fuel sold as LPG — what compound is it?
Propane is a three-carbon chain alkane with the molecular formula C3H8.

Distinguished from their smaller rodent cousins mainly by size, these long-tailed rodents span dozens of genera worldwide, with Rattus being the most familiar — of the 56 known species, what are they collectively called?
Rat are various medium-sized, long-tailed rodents.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrographs, this virus is the leading cause of diarrheal disease in infants worldwide, spread via the fecal-oral route — what is it?
Rotavirus are the most common cause of diarrhoeal disease among infants and young children.
This marine plant group includes kelp, captures carbon, and generates over half of the planet's oxygen — what is it called?
Seaweed refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.
Doctors recommend covering your elbow rather than your hands to block this involuntary, explosive rush of air from spreading illness through the air. What is this reflex called?
Sneeze (also known as sternutation) is a semi-autonomous, convulsive expulsion of air from the lungs through the nose and mouth, usually caused by foreign particles irritating the nasal mucosa.
A Canadian cognitive psychologist at Harvard who champions evolutionary psychology and the computational theory of mind, which popular-science author wrote on how children learn irregular verb forms?
Steven Pinker (born September 18, 1954) is a Canadian cognitive psychologist, psycholinguist, popular science author, and public intellectual.
Symbol Tc, atomic number 43: this silvery-gray metal is entirely synthetic, though tiny natural traces form via neutron capture in molybdenum ore — what element?
Technetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
A staple of Mexican cuisine grown as an annual despite being naturally perennial, this small green-purple fruit is best known for flavoring salsa verde — what is it?
Tomatillo (Physalis philadelphica and Physalis ixocarpa), also known as the Mexican husk tomato, is a plant of the nightshade family bearing small, spherical, and green or green-purple fruit.

This membrane-bound organelle, found in plant and fungal cells and some others, is essentially a water-filled storage compartment with no fixed shape, formed when smaller membrane vesicles fuse together. What is it called?
Vacuole is a membrane-bound organelle which is present in plant and fungal cells and some protist, animal, and bacterial cells.

This American physical chemist built ultra-sensitive Geiger counters and once worked on the Manhattan Project — but his 1960 Nobel came for a dating method that revolutionized archaeology and paleontology. Who was he?

Willard Libby (December 17, 1908 - September 8, 1980) was an American physical chemist noted for his role in the 1949 development of radiocarbon dating, a process which revolutionized archaeology and palaeontology.

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
Native to China and Taiwan, this fast-growing deciduous tree can reach 15 meters in 25 years and has become notorious in North America as a host plant for the invasive spotted lanternfly. What is it?
Ailanthus altissima: Deciduous tree in the quassia family.
Prized for its oil since Spanish and Portuguese traders carried it from South America to Europe in the 1600s, this citrus-scented herb also goes by 'beebrush' — what's its species name?
Aloysia citrodora: Species of plant. Aloysia citrodora, lemon verbena, is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family Verbenaceae, native to South America.
This English mathematician earned a knighthood and the Abel Prize for proving Fermat's Last Theorem, a problem that fascinated him since childhood in Nigeria. Who is he?
Andrew Wiles: British mathematician who proved Fermat's Last Theorem.
This inflammatory condition causes right lower abdominal pain and is commonly triggered by a blockage from a calcified mass of feces called a fecalith — what is it?

Often called a 'collapsed lung' in casual speech, this condition is really the partial deflation of the lung's alveoli rather than fluid filling them, and shows up frequently on chest X-rays — what is it?
Atelectasis: Partial collapse of a lung causing reduced gas exchange.
A tender herb of the mint family native from Central Africa to Southeast Asia, its Genovese or 'sweet' variety is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Basil: Culinary herb. Basil (Ocimum basilicum), also called great basil, is a culinary herb of the family Lamiaceae (mints).
Also known as vitamin B7, this B vitamin is found in every living cell and is popularly sold as a supplement; isolated, it's a white needle-like crystal — what is it?
Biotin: Chemical compound and essential nutrient.
Certified in Canada in 1998, this large-cabin business jet shares its fuselage cross-section with the Challenger 600 and first flew in 1996 — which jet is it?
Bombardier Global Express: Large cabin business jet. The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation.

Comprising over 250 species that form small colonies of as few as 50 individuals around a single queen, these fuzzy insects were introduced to New Zealand and Tasmania and can sting repeatedly without dying — which insect is it?
Bumblebee: Genus of insect. A bumblebee (or bumble bee, bumble-bee, or humble-bee) is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, part of Apidae, one of the bee families.
Designated Alpha Carinae and located some 310 light-years away, this bright giant is the second-brightest star in the night sky, outshone only by Sirius — which star?
Canopus: Brightest star in the constellation of Carina.
A first-generation cephalosporin and β-lactam, this antibiotic can be taken by mouth and treats ear, bone, skin and urinary infections by disrupting bacterial cell-wall growth — what is it?
Cefalexin: Beta-lactam antibiotic. Cefalexin, also spelled cephalexin, is an antibiotic that can treat a number of bacterial infections.
Nicknamed the sea wasp, this Australian box jellyfish is considered the world's most lethal, with venom-laced tentacles up to 10 feet long — which species?
Chironex fleckeri: Species of jellyfish. It has been described as "the most lethal jellyfish in the world", with at least 64 known deaths in Australia from 1884 to 2021.
Discovered in 1969 and sold under the brand name Lotrimin, this azole-class medication treats athlete's foot, ringworm, and oral thrush — what is it?

Native to the western Palearctic and closely related to the rock dove, this large bird feeds mainly on cereals and other plant matter, making it an agricultural pest despite being heavily hunted across its range — what is it?
Common wood pigeon: Species of large, white/green-naped, arboreal bird of Eurasia.
This genus of some 100 low-growing perennials gives us saffron from the dried stigmas of one autumn-blooming species — name the flower genus?
This basic unit of time — averaging 24 hours, or 86,400 seconds — marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun, and got split into weeks, months, and years. What is it?
Day: Time of one rotation around a planet axis.

Governed since 1961 by the Vienna Convention, this practice of using official representatives to influence international relations became a professionalized field in the early 20th century. What is it?
Diplomacy: Practice of conducting negotiations between representatives of groups or states.
This condition involves involuntarily repeating words or sounds spoken by someone else, and is commonly seen in autism, ADHD, and Tourette syndrome. What is it called?
Often triggered by contaminated food, NSAIDs, or autoimmune conditions like coeliac disease, which medical term describes inflammation of the small intestine?
Enteritis: Inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.

With a wingspan reaching 188 centimeters and distinctive ear tufts atop mottled blackish-and-tawny plumage, this raptor is one of the largest of its nocturnal kind, ranging widely across Europe and Asia — what bird is it?
Eurasian eagle-owl: Species of owl. The Eurasian eagle-owl (Bubo bubo) is a species of eagle-owl, a type of bird that resides much over Eurasia.
First synthesized by Paul Janssen in 1960 and sold under brand names like Duragesic, this synthetic opioid runs 50 to 100 times more potent than morphine — what is it?
Fentanyl: Opioid medication. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.

Madagascar's largest carnivore is a slender, long-tailed mammal that climbs down trees head-first and has convergently evolved so many cat-like features it's been likened to a small cougar — yet it's no cat. What is it?
Fossa (animal): Cat-like, carnivorous mammal endemic to Madagascar.
This field studies the relationship between food and culture, encompassing everything from cooking techniques and regional cuisines to the science of good eating — what is it called?

Gastronomy: Study of the relationship between food and culture. One who is well versed in gastronomy is called a gastronome, while a gastronomist is one who unites theory and practice in the study of gastronomy.
The most abundant free amino acid in human blood, this one is named after the compound found in gluten and is coded for by the codons CAA and CAG — what is it?
Glutamine: Amino acid. Glutamine (symbol Gln or Q) is an α-amino acid that is used in the biosynthesis of proteins.

Beginning as weakness in the feet and hands before spreading upward, this rapid-onset autoimmune condition attacks the peripheral nervous system and can require a ventilator in about 15% of cases — which disorder is this?
Guillain–Barré syndrome: Autoimmune disease. Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.
Nicknamed a 'strawberry mark' in infants, this usually benign vascular tumor tends to grow for about a year before gradually shrinking — what is it?
Hemangioma: Vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Arching shrubs or twining vines in the genus Lonicera, some 158 species of this fragrant plant attract hummingbirds in North America — what is it?
This psychiatric state brings a surge of energy, euphoria, and a reduced need for sleep — milder than its more severe cousin because it doesn't significantly impair daily functioning — what is it?

A former Communist Party official who was later sidelined by Nicolae Ceaușescu, this engineer-turned-politician emerged from Romania's 1989 revolution to become the country's first freely elected president — who is he?
After a cross-country road trip from New York to Seattle, this Princeton engineering graduate founded an online bookstore in 1994 that grew into a global e-commerce giant. Who is he?
This twin-engine fighter jet program made its home nation the fourth in the world to develop stealth avionics, joining the ranks of the US, China, and Russia — which aircraft?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: South Korean fighter aircraft.
Situated between two larger folds of skin, these paired flaps extend from the inner vaginal and urethral openings and form the clitoral hood above — which structures are these?
Labia minora: Flaps of skin on either side of the vaginal opening in the vulva.

Elon Musk's praise for his MIT driver-attention study on Tesla's autopilot brought this computer scientist to prominence in 2019, ahead of a career hosting long-form interviews with notable figures — who is he?
Lex Fridman: American scientist and podcast host (born 1983)
Sold as Ativan, this benzodiazepine treats anxiety, insomnia, and active seizures, and is even used during surgery to interfere with memory formation — what medication is it?
Lorazepam: Benzodiazepine medication. Lorazepam, sold under the brand name Ativan among others, is a benzodiazepine medication.
This genus of some 32 to 57 deciduous tree and shrub species in the rose family includes the domesticated orchard fruit tree along with crab and wild varieties — what genus is it?
Malus: Flowering genus, rose family Rosaceae.

The largest trijet ever built, this American wide-body airliner first flew in January 1990 and entered service with Finnair that December, a stretched, winglet-equipped update of an earlier trijet — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-11: Wide body airliners developed from the DC-10.
A physician-turned-hedge-fund-manager, this investor famously predicted the subprime mortgage crisis and was portrayed in the 2015 film The Big Short — who is he?
Michael Burry: American hedge fund manager (born 1971)
With shovel-like front limbs built for burrowing and a mating song broadcast from a specially shaped underground tunnel, which insect is this?
Mole cricket: Members of the insect family Gryllotalpidae.
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.
This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not Earth, at the center of the universe in a book published just before his death in 1543 — kicking off a revolution in science. Who was he?
Known as holy basil and sacred within the Vaishnava tradition of Hinduism, which aromatic herb is widely used in Ayurvedic tea?
Ocimum tenuiflorum: Species of flowering plant.

Most members of this order of over 200 species are solitary night hunters with broad heads, binocular vision, and feathers tuned for silent flight — though oddballs like the burrowing kind break the mold. What are they?
Owl: Birds from the order Strigiformes.
One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory and famously preferred cracking open problems to building grand theories — who was he?
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?

Often at its worst with the very first steps of the day, this common foot disorder inflames the connective tissue supporting the arch and is linked to tight calf muscles and heel spurs — what condition is it?

Plantar fasciitis: Connective tissue disorder of the heel. Plantar fasciitis or plantar heel pain is a disorder of the plantar fascia, which is the connective tissue that supports the arch of the foot.
Sold under the brand name Lyrica, this anticonvulsant amino-acid drug also treats fibromyalgia, nerve pain, and anxiety — which medication is it?
Pregabalin: Anticonvulsant medication. Its use in epilepsy is as an add-on therapy for partial seizures.
Named by the medieval scholar Gerard of Cremona, this black-looking opening in the eye's iris is round in humans but a vertical slit in cats and a horizontal bar in goats — what is it?
Pupil: Part of an eye. The pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.

A canine native to the southeastern United States, intermediate in size between the coyote and gray wolf. For a century its status as a separate species has been debated — some call it a coywolf. Name this animal.
Red wolf: Canid native to the southeastern United States. Fish and Wildlife Service recognizes the red wolf as an endangered species and grants it protected status.
A Jesuit priest and polymath from the Republic of Ragusa produced an early precursor of atomic theory and, in 1753, discovered that the Moon has no atmosphere — who was he?
Roger Joseph Boscovich: Croat-Italian physicist and writer (1711–1787)
